# Agent identity configuration reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_agent_identity_reference.py; do not edit by hand. -->

Policy schema version: 1.

The optional `agent_identity` root is read from effective profile configuration. An absent root or an empty mapping preserves legacy behavior. Any other malformed value fails closed before provider construction. There is no environment-variable or display-name override and no `enabled` switch.

## Root: agent_identity

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | `int` | yes | Opt-in identity schema version; currently 1 |
| `principal_id` | `str` | yes | Immutable configured owner identifier |
| `profile_id` | `str` | yes | Immutable configured profile identifier, distinct from its home path |
| `primary_agent_id` | `str` | yes | The sole configured primary identity |
| `active_agent_id` | `str` | yes | Configured stable identity used for new top-level sessions |
| `agents` | `Mapping[str, AgentPolicy]` | yes | Configured stable agent IDs mapped to AgentPolicy records |
| `child_policy` | `AgentPolicy \| None` | no | Explicit child/builtin ceiling; absent or null denies child construction |
| `personal_mcp_servers` | `frozenset[str]` | no | Personal harness server inventory; grants are restricted to the primary |
| `personal_secret_refs` | `frozenset[str]` | no | Personal harness credential reference inventory; restricted to the primary |

## Policy: agents.<configured-id> and child_policy

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy_version` | `int` | yes | Policy contract version; currently 1 |
| `role` | `Literal['primary', 'specialist', 'child']` | yes | primary for the sole primary ID; specialist for configured peers; child for child_policy |
| `memory_backend` | `Literal['personal_mcp', 'builtin']` | yes | personal_mcp for primary only; builtin for every specialist and child |

| `secret_refs` | `frozenset[str]` | no | Exact credential reference names, never credential values |
| `project_grants` | `frozenset[str]` | no | Reserved project grant list; must be empty until BE07 enforcement |
| `egress_purposes` | `frozenset[str]` | no | Reserved egress purpose list; must be empty until BE05 enforcement |

## Identity and lifecycle rules

- Principal, profile, agent and session IDs must match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}`; Windows reserved device names are rejected. IDs cannot contain paths, dots or spaces.
- Exactly `primary_agent_id` has the primary role and personal_mcp backend. All other configured IDs have specialist role and builtin backend.
- The `child_` agent namespace is reserved. Trusted construction generates `child_<32 lowercase hex>` IDs; model names and prompts cannot choose one.
- A child requires its parent context and an explicit child_policy. Its grants are the intersection of parent grants and child policy, including MCP tools and secrets. Project and egress collections must remain empty in BE01.
- Personal MCP servers and personal credential references are forbidden in every specialist and child policy, even when profiles are shared.
- Grant names are exact and case-sensitive. Wildcards and duplicate grants are rejected. Missing grant collections are empty, never allow-all. An MCP server with no granted tools is not admitted.
- Unknown fields, unsupported versions, type errors and unknown active/primary IDs are rejected. Inventory fields on resolved policies are derived from configuration and cannot be supplied as policy grants.

## Resume, redaction and scope

Bindings store identity IDs, lifecycle, parent ID, binding revision, policy/config digests and a home digest. An existing session with no binding is refused under enabled policy. A mismatched session ID, changed policy/configuration, home or active agent also refuses resume. Starting a new session is the explicit migration boundary; newer records never downgrade to legacy access.

AgentContext is frozen and contains only its binding, policy, config digest and canonical profile home. Redacted inspection includes provenance and credential-reference counts, never credential values or raw configuration. Bind/read validate the current effective home; contextvars preserve identity across copy_context thread hops. Profile lifecycle code must bind home, secrets and terminal policy together before installing identity.

Configuration changes apply at the next construction/session boundary. The current conversation's policy and prompt remain immutable. Restoring a saved session requires its original compatible binding.

## Enforcement boundaries

These contracts describe authority, not an OS sandbox. Nonempty egress_purposes and project_grants are rejected until BE05/BE07 provide concrete dispatch enforcement. This phase does not implement personal MCP memory semantics or specialist memory persistence; those are BE08 dependencies. No raw AIAgent, secret dictionary or generic service locator is exposed by AgentContext.

## Regeneration

Run `.venv/bin/python scripts/gen_agent_identity_reference.py` after schema changes. Use `--check` to verify freshness without writing. The focused identity tests compare this reference with the current typed schema.
